description: A graduate course on measuring cyber risk with probability and loss models, and on why security decisions are shaped by incentives, markets and strategic adversaries. Students build Monte Carlo loss models and game-theoretic defences in the maths lab, and defend investment decisions in scored scenarios.
modelledOn: Freund and Jones, Measuring and Managing Information Risk: A FAIR Approach
Hubbard and Seiersen, How to Measure Anything in Cybersecurity Risk
outcomes: Build a quantitative risk model from frequency and severity distributions and report a loss exceedance curve with uncertainty.
Construct attack trees and attack graphs and compute attack probabilities and cheapest attack paths.
Estimate breach losses and evaluate cyber insurance terms, including accumulation and moral hazard.
Analyse security investment with cost-benefit models and explain externalities and information asymmetry.
Model attacker and defender choices as games and compute equilibria and optimal mixed defences.
Present a risk decision to a board with transparent assumptions, metrics and sensitivity analysis.

units.title: Foundations of cyber risk
topics: Assets, threats, vulnerabilities and risk as likelihood times impact
Qualitative versus quantitative assessment; the flaws of risk matrices
Probability toolkit: distributions, Bayes' rule and Monte Carlo simulation
Frameworks: ISO 27005, NIST risk management and the FAIR taxonomy
Risk appetite, tolerance and treatment options: avoid, reduce, transfer, accept

units.title: Quantitative risk models
topics: FAIR decomposition: loss event frequency and loss magnitude
Frequency-severity modelling: Poisson counts and lognormal or Pareto losses
Monte Carlo aggregation, loss exceedance curves, value at risk and expected shortfall
Bayesian updating with sparse incident data; calibrated expert elicitation
Dependence and aggregation: correlation and copulas
Sensitivity analysis and model risk

units.title: Attack trees and threat modelling
topics: STRIDE threat modelling on data-flow diagrams
Attack trees with AND/OR nodes: probability, cost and cheapest attack
Attack graphs and Bayesian attack graphs
Kill chains and the ATT&CK matrix as a threat catalogue
Markov models of compromise and attacker progress
Quantifying detection and response: time to detect and time to contain

units.title: Loss estimation and insurance
topics: Breach cost components: direct, indirect, regulatory and reputational loss
Cyber insurance: coverage, exclusions, premium setting and actuarial pricing
Systemic risk and accumulation from shared cloud and software dependencies
Moral hazard and adverse selection in cyber insurance
Case: mobile money fraud losses and recovery in West Africa

units.title: Incentives and security investment
topics: Security investment models with diminishing returns and the one-third rule of thumb
Return on security investment, NPV and budget allocation
Externalities, free riding and security as a public good; weakest-link versus best-shot
Information asymmetry, the market for lemons and certification
Behavioural economics: compliance budgets, usability and phishing
Regulation, liability and data protection law as incentives

units.title: Game-theoretic defence models
topics: Normal-form games, Nash equilibrium and mixed strategies
Stackelberg security games and optimal randomised patrols or scans
Inspection games, deception and honeypots
Dynamic and Bayesian games; signalling and incomplete information
Timing games for stealthy takeover and key rotation
Bounded rationality and learning in games

units.title: Vulnerability markets and disclosure
topics: Vulnerability scoring and prediction: CVSS and exploit prediction scoring
Vulnerability lifecycle and the economics of patching
Bug bounties and exploit markets
Coordinated disclosure policy and national reporting rules

units.title: Security metrics and decision making
topics: Leading and lagging security metrics; metric gaming and perverse incentives
Decision analysis: expected utility and the value of information
Communicating uncertainty to a board
Capstone risk assessment and investment recommendation

schedule.title: Risk concepts and measurement
schedule.exercise: List the assets, threats and vulnerabilities of a mobile money agent network, score five risks on a 5x5 matrix, then show two different risks that the matrix ranks identically but differ greatly in expected loss.

tasks.title: Identify assets, threats and vulnerabilities in a clinic records case and rank six risks by likelihood times impact using the evidence given
Score eight risks on a 5x5 matrix, compute expected losses from given ranges, and show two risks whose matrix cells hide a tenfold difference
Simulate 10,000 years of incidents with a Poisson frequency and lognormal loss, and report the mean, 95th percentile and chance of a loss above a given limit

schedule.title: Frameworks and risk treatment
schedule.exercise: Map a risk assessment of a district hospital onto the steps of two frameworks, then choose a treatment for each of six risks and justify the residual risk against a stated appetite.

tasks.title: Order the steps of a risk assessment process from context to monitoring for a case, and match each to the corresponding framework activity
Pick a treatment option for six risks in a case under a fixed budget, and compute the residual risk against the stated appetite
Decompose a ransomware risk into FAIR factors, set ranges for each and compute the distribution of annualised loss with a short sensitivity table

schedule.title: FAIR, frequency and severity
schedule.exercise: Fit a Poisson frequency and a lognormal severity to a small incident log, simulate annual loss and read the loss exceedance curve at 1 in 10 and 1 in 100 year levels.

tasks.title: Break a data-breach scenario into loss event frequency and loss magnitude components and fill in a minimum, likely and maximum for each
Fit a Poisson distribution to monthly incident counts and a lognormal to loss sizes, then check each fit with a goodness measure
Aggregate 50,000 simulated years of losses, plot the loss exceedance curve and compute the value at risk and expected shortfall at 99 percent

schedule.title: Bayesian estimates, dependence and model risk
schedule.exercise: Update a prior estimate of breach frequency after two quiet years, aggregate two correlated risks with a copula, and rank the inputs of a loss model by their influence on the 95th percentile.

tasks.title: Combine a prior on annual breach probability with two years of no incidents using a beta update, and plot prior and posterior
Simulate two risks with correlation 0, 0.5 and 0.9, and show how the 99th percentile of the combined loss changes
Run a one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis on a loss model with six inputs, rank them for the tail loss and name the assumption most worth gathering data on

schedule.title: STRIDE, attack trees and attack graphs
schedule.exercise: Draw a data-flow diagram for a mobile money app, list STRIDE threats for each element, build an attack tree for fraudulent cash-out and find the cheapest attack path.

tasks.title: Draw a data-flow diagram of a mobile money transfer and list one STRIDE threat for each process, store, flow and trust boundary
Build an attack tree with AND and OR nodes for stealing a SIM identity, assign costs and probabilities, and compute the cheapest path
Convert a six-host network into an attack graph with exploit probabilities, compute the probability of reaching the database and rank the best patch

schedule.title: Kill chains, Markov models and response time
schedule.exercise: Map an incident report onto kill chain stages, model attacker progress as a Markov chain, and estimate how faster detection changes expected loss.

tasks.title: Map twelve events from an incident timeline to kill chain stages and mark where a detection control would have interrupted the attack
Model an intrusion as a five-state Markov chain, compute the chance of full compromise within 30 days and the mean time to absorb
Simulate loss growth per day of undetected presence, and compare expected loss for mean detection times of 5, 20 and 60 days

schedule.title: Breach losses and cyber insurance
schedule.exercise: Price a cyber insurance policy from a loss distribution with a deductible and limit, show how a shared cloud outage creates accumulation, and explain moral hazard in a policy with no security conditions.

tasks.title: Itemise the direct, indirect and regulatory costs of a customer data breach for a Ghanaian retailer and total them with ranges
Compute the expected insurer payout for a policy with a deductible and limit from a simulated loss distribution, and set a premium with a 30 percent load
Simulate 1,000 insured firms sharing one cloud provider, compare independent and common-shock losses, and show how reserves for the portfolio change

schedule.title: Security investment and incentives
schedule.exercise: Compute the optimal security spend for a vulnerability under a diminishing-returns breach probability function, then explain why firms in a weakest-link network underinvest.

tasks.title: Compute return on security investment and NPV for three controls from given costs and avoided loss, and rank them
Plot expected net benefit against spend under a diminishing-returns breach function, find the optimum and compare it with the rule of thumb
Simulate 20 firms choosing security effort in a weakest-link network, compare the equilibrium with the social optimum and quantify the gap

schedule.title: Information asymmetry, behaviour and regulation
schedule.exercise: Explain how a market for security products can fall into a lemons market, estimate the compliance budget of staff facing frequent warnings, and compare fines and liability rules as incentives.

tasks.title: Judge three product claims in a procurement case with limited evidence, and choose which vendor to trust using certification information
Design a phishing awareness programme in a branching case, set training and policy choices, and compare click rates over simulated quarters
Model a firm's security spend under no rule, a fixed fine and a strict liability rule, and show which one best aligns its incentive with social cost

schedule.title: Games, Nash equilibrium and Stackelberg models
schedule.exercise: Solve a 3x3 attacker-defender matrix game for its mixed equilibrium, compute the leader's optimal randomised strategy in a Stackelberg version, and compare the two.

tasks.title: Find pure and mixed Nash equilibria of a 2x2 attacker-defender game with given payoffs and check that no player gains by deviating
Compute the defender's optimal randomised coverage of four targets against an attacker who observes the strategy, and compare it with uniform coverage
Model a honeypot deployment as a deception game, compute the equilibrium mix of real and fake systems and report the defender payoff

schedule.title: Dynamic games, timing and bounded rationality
schedule.exercise: Analyse a signalling game between a vendor and a buyer, find the best key-rotation interval against a stealthy attacker, and discuss how a boundedly rational attacker changes the equilibrium.

tasks.title: Solve a two-type signalling game by backward induction and state under which beliefs a separating equilibrium holds
Simulate a stealthy takeover game with periodic key rotation and find the rotation interval that maximises the defender's control share
Simulate learning attackers using fictitious play against a defender, plot strategy convergence and compare it with the computed equilibrium

schedule.title: Vulnerability markets and disclosure
schedule.exercise: Prioritise twenty vulnerabilities using severity and exploit likelihood, estimate the cost of patching delays, and compare a bounty programme with an exploit broker market.

tasks.title: Rank twenty vulnerabilities by severity alone and by severity times exploit probability, and list those whose rank changes most
Model patch timing as a trade-off between exposure and outage risk, and find the patch delay that minimises expected cost
Decide how to disclose a flaw found in a national payment gateway in a branching case, balancing user harm, vendor response and legal duties

schedule.title: Metrics, decisions and capstone
schedule.exercise: Prepare a board paper that recommends a security budget for a regional bank, with a loss exceedance curve, sensitivity analysis, alternatives and the expected value of better information.

tasks.title: Sort twelve proposed security metrics into leading and lagging indicators, and identify two that would invite gaming
Compute the expected value of perfect information for a choice between two controls and decide whether a 20,000 cedi audit is worth buying
Recommend a security investment plan to a simulated board, answer questions on assumptions and uncertainty, and revise the plan against the rubric
